{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABinGgXg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhL9u2w", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 241, "title": "Enable sound by default and resume playback after returning to a visible tab", "body": "## Problem

The browser player currently starts with `muted = true` in [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js). Audio is initialized through the sound button, so a user can start playing without realizing sound is disabled. The existing `visibilitychange` handler pauses the running guest when the document becomes hidden, but returns immediately when the document becomes visible again. Users have to resume manually after switching tabs.

The maintainer requests two ordinary-use improvements: **sound on by default**, and **automatic resume after a visibility-induced pause, without overriding a deliberate user pause**.

## 1. Enable audio by default

- Default the user's sound preference to enabled and retain the existing default volume of 100%. Initialize the existing AudioContext/AudioWorklet path automatically when the browser allows it.
- Respect browser autoplay policy. If audible playback cannot start without user activation, leave the guest usable and automatically attempt audio initialization/resume on the first suitable trusted click/tap or keyboard interaction (including clicking the guest screen for Pointer Lock). Call resume within the activation handler before asynchronous work that might lose activation. Do not require a separate click on the sound button. Avoid blocking startup on a suspended context or an unresolved resume promise.
- Distinguish desired sound state from actual AudioContext availability/running state. Keep the sound control and any compact status truthful; if autoplay is blocked, show a brief actionable indication when necessary, not a disruptive dialog.
- Explicit mute/unmute and volume changes remain available. Do not automatically unmute after user mute, including on tab return or later interactions. A zero volume must remain zero. Keep the existing stereo playback, sample rates, bounded audio queue and reset/pause semantics; do not change guest timing or synthesize fake audio.

## 2. Automatically resume after switching back to the tab

- Keep the current auto-pause policy when `document.hidden` becomes true. Remember whether the guest was running and was paused specifically because of the visibility change.
- On return to a visible document, automatically resume only a guest that was running before the visibility-induced pause, provided it is still safe/eligible to run.
- If the user explicitly paused the guest, keep it paused across tab changes. Do not resume a stopped/faulted guest, a machine without boot media, or an unfinished disk import/save/export/reset transaction. Preserve normal transaction completion semantics and avoid stale resume requests when the machine or user intent changes.
- Handle audio context suspension/interruption on return using the same sound intent and browser permissions; if necessary retry on a suitable user gesture. Never override explicit mute.
- Preserve input release and Pointer Lock safety when hiding the tab; returning must not automatically recapture the mouse. Avoid catch-up bursts or stale queued audio after resuming.

## Implementation scope

Primarily `web/app.js` (initial sound state, `enableAudio`, `soundState`, `setRunning`, pause button, `visibilitychange`), plus the corresponding sound-control defaults in `web/index.html` and relevant browser tests/Help. Prefer a small clear separation of user playback intent, visibility suspension and effective running state. Reuse the existing Worker/AudioWorklet and media transaction APIs. Do not introduce new UI settings, change the Rust core, redesign audio scheduling, or alter HDD persistence.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance (bounded)

- [ ] In a browser allowing autoplay, sound starts enabled without clicking a dedicated enable button. With autoplay blocked, a normal trusted user interaction enables audio automatically; explicit mute and volume are respected. Verify actual guest-generated audio, not only UI labels.
- [ ] A running guest pauses when hidden and resumes on becoming visible; a manually paused guest remains paused. Check actual guest progress and a representative audio-enabled run.
- [ ] No unintended resume of a stopped guest or during media operations, no surprise mouse recapture, and no regression of ordinary pause/resume, sound controls, boot/reset, HDD save/restore or audio continuity.
- [ ] Add focused browser regressions and run applicable existing required checks at both serving roots. Update Help if needed. Use existing successful evidence for unaffected functionality; do not require exhaustive browser/OS/autoplay or race-case permutations.

**Completion boundary:** the two normal-use workflows above are the goal. Browser autoplay restrictions are not a defect if gesture-based activation works; minor platform-specific limitations can be documented as nonblocking. Fix actual major regressions and required-check failures, but do not prolong this Issue for speculative edge cases or unrelated refinements.

Related: #136 (Worker/audio), #233 (player UI), #235 (Pointer Lock), #237 (HDD persistence), #239 (HDD controls).

## Required post-merge verification
